title: Cofiltered coherent diagrams whose arrows are equivalences
statement:
Fix universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty ordinary category such that any two objects receive arrows from a common object and every parallel pair $f,g:i\to j$ is equalized by some arrow $k\to i$. Let $\mathscr C$ be an enhanced category in the larger universe (a category retaining mapping spaces and all composition homotopies, equivalently an infinity category), using the precise coherent-diagram and cone conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A coherent diagram on $I$ consists of its objects, arrows, composition homotopies for strings of arrows and all higher compatibilities, i.e. a functor from the nerve $N(I)$ to $\mathscr C$. Write $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{eq}}(N(I),\mathscr C)$ for the full enhanced subcategory of diagrams sending every arrow of $I$ to an equivalence. Then the constant-diagram functor
$$\mathscr C\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{eq}}(N(I),\mathscr C)$$
is an equivalence; evaluation at any fixed object of $I$ is an inverse equivalence. For each such diagram $F$, its homotopy limit exists and every projection $\operatorname{holim}_I F\to F(i)$ is an equivalence. The space of limiting cones is contractible. These constructions are natural for coherent transformations of diagrams and for changes of indexing category between nonempty cofiltered categories. The same assertions hold for filtered categories and homotopy colimits. They apply also when $\mathscr C$ is an enhanced functor category, so that the cones and equivalences are natural in its parameters. No assertion is made about diagrams having noninvertible arrows or about the empty index category.

source.place: Tag 04AZ, label definition-codirected, supplies the precise nonempty/common-predecessor/equalizer hypotheses only. The contractibility of the nerve and the enhanced constant-diagram and limiting-cone assertions are additional agent-formulated foundations. WANTED: weak contractibility of filtered nerves and the universal property of groupoid completion in enhanced categories.

proof.text: Put $K=N(I)$, in the terminology of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The nonemptiness, common-predecessor and actual parallel-arrow equalizer hypotheses of the item are exactly the cofiltered alternative in [lem-cbc-filtered-nerve-weak-contractibility]. Thus the unique map $p:K\to\Delta^0$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. This is a statement about all homotopy groups; replacing it by mere connectedness would not suffice.

source.place: Proof opening compactification choice: generic enhanced choice-independence argument (agent).

proof.text: The target $\Delta^0$ is Kan: there is exactly one map from each simplex or horn to it, and it extends uniquely. Apply [lem-cbc-simplicial-groupoid-localization] to $p$. Since $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^0,\mathscr C)=\mathscr C$, the resulting functor $p^*$ is exactly $\Delta_I:\mathscr C\to E_I:=\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{eq}}(N(I),\mathscr C)$. It is an equivalence of enhanced categories on objects and on the entire mapping spaces of coherent transformations. The functor and full subcategory are enhanced categories by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus].

source.place: Proof opening compactification choice: generic enhanced choice-independence argument (agent).

proof.text: For any chosen $i\in I$, evaluation $e_i:E_I\to\mathscr C$ satisfies $e_i\Delta_I=\mathrm{id}$. To exhibit its other inverse equation, choose a quasi-inverse $L_I$ to the equivalence in step 2, with natural equivalence $\alpha:\Delta_I L_I\simeq\mathrm{id}_{E_I}$. Applying $e_i$ gives $L_I\simeq e_i$; applying $\Delta_I$ to the inverse of this equivalence and then composing with $\alpha$ gives $\Delta_I e_i\simeq\mathrm{id}_{E_I}$. These are coherent transformations because all operations take place in the functor categories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Thus every evaluation is an inverse equivalence. In particular each component of $\alpha_F$ is an equivalence, by componentwise detection in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus].

source.place: Proof opening compactification choice: generic enhanced choice-independence argument (agent).

proof.text:
For $F\in E_I$, regard $\alpha_F:\Delta_I(L_IF)\simeq F$ as a cone. For each $x\in\mathscr C$, its universal map on mapping spaces factors as
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathscr C}(x,L_IF)\xrightarrow{\Delta_I}\operatorname{Map}_{E_I}(\Delta_Ix,\Delta_I L_IF)\xrightarrow{\alpha_F\circ-}\operatorname{Map}_{E_I}(\Delta_Ix,F).$$
The first map is an equivalence because $\Delta_I$ is an equivalence; the second has inverse given by postcomposition with $\alpha_F^{-1}$; the two inverse equations follow by composing with $\alpha_F^{-1}\alpha_F\simeq\mathrm{id}$ and $\alpha_F\alpha_F^{-1}\simeq\mathrm{id}$. Fullness identifies the last mapping space with that in all of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathscr C)$. These are precisely the maps in the cone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], so this cone is limiting. Its projection at $i$ is $(\alpha_F)_i:L_IF\to F(i)$, already an equivalence. No general existence of $I$-limits in $\mathscr C$ has been assumed.

source.place: Proof opening compactification choice: generic enhanced choice-independence argument (agent).

proof.text: The limiting cones on the fixed diagram $F$ are exactly the terminal objects of its coherent cone category. Its terminal-object subcategory is nonempty by step 4. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], the full subcategory of its terminal objects is a contractible Kan complex. Thus the space of limiting cones, including their apices and comparison homotopies, is contractible. Any other limiting cone is equivalent to the one from step 4 in the cone category. Its projections are therefore composites, up to the cone compatibility homotopies, of equivalences of apices with the projections in step 4, hence are equivalences as well.

source.place: Proof opening compactification choice: generic enhanced choice-independence argument (agent).

proof.text: The quasi-inverse $L_I$ and equivalence $\alpha:\Delta_I L_I\simeq\mathrm{id}_{E_I}$ from step 3 already form a coherent family on all of $E_I$. For a transformation $t:F\to H$, its naturality homotopy is $t\alpha_F\simeq\alpha_H\Delta_I(L_It)$, with all higher simplices supplied by $\alpha$. This proves naturality in diagram transformations without choosing separate maps between individual limits.

source.place: Opening compactification choice: diagram naturality from the chosen coherent equivalence.

proof.text:
Let $u:J\to I$ be any functor between nonempty cofiltered categories. Repeating steps 1-2 for $J$ makes $\Delta_J:\mathscr C\to E_J$ fully faithful. Restriction satisfies $u^*\Delta_I=\Delta_J$, and $u^*\alpha_F:\Delta_J L_IF\simeq u^*F$ is an equivalence. The mapping-space map of this restricted cone factors as
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathscr C}(x,L_IF)\xrightarrow{\Delta_J}\operatorname{Map}_{E_J}(\Delta_Jx,\Delta_J L_IF)\xrightarrow{u^*\alpha_F\circ-}\operatorname{Map}_{E_J}(\Delta_Jx,u^*F).$$
Both maps are equivalences, the second with inverse postcomposition by $(u^*\alpha_F)^{-1}$. Fullness of $E_J$ and the cone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] show that restriction preserves this limiting cone. Every other limiting cone is equivalent to this one by step 5; restriction preserves its inverse equations, and the cone criterion is invariant under such a cone equivalence. Thus restriction preserves every limiting cone on these diagrams.

source.place: Opening compactification choice: restriction preserves the displayed universal cones; explicit mapping-space calculation.

proof.text: Enlarge the universe to contain $P=E_I$. The universal $J$-diagram in $\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathscr C)$ sends $j$ to $F\mapsto F(u(j))$. Two coherent cones on it have apices $L_I$ and $L_Ju^*$, with transformations $u^*\alpha_I$ and $\alpha_Ju^*$. Evaluation at each $F$ gives limiting cones by steps 7 and 4. Apply the general pointwise limit criterion in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]: the corresponding individual limits exist because these cones exhibit them; completeness of $\mathscr C$ is not required. Both cones are therefore terminal in the same coherent cone category in $\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathscr C)$. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] their space of cone-compatible comparisons is contractible and every comparison is an equivalence. Its apex map is the desired $L_I\to L_Ju^*$, as a coherent natural transformation on all of $P$, including noninvertible arrows and higher simplices.

source.place: Opening compactification choice: parameterized universal-cone comparison; generic pointwise theorem, also Kerodon 02X9 and its limit dual.

proof.text: For $v:H\to J$, restriction of cone data satisfies $(uv)^*=v^*u^*$ in every degree by the internal functor formulas of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. In $\operatorname{Fun}(E_I,\mathscr C)$, the restricted $I$-cone, restricted $J$-cone and chosen $H$-cone are all limiting cones on the same $H$-diagram, by steps 7-8. The comparison for $u$, restricted along $v$, and the comparison for $v$ are edges in their full terminal-object subcategory $T$. The direct comparison for $uv$ is another such edge. The calculus makes $T$ a contractible Kan complex. Therefore $T\to\Delta^0$ is a Kan fibration and a weak homotopy equivalence, and [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion] makes it a trivial Kan fibration. Its boundary lifting supplies the triangle relating the two successive comparisons to the direct one. Take identity comparisons to be degenerate edges. Inductively, for a string of index functors, the lower-dimensional compatibilities give a boundary in the corresponding terminal-cone space, after restriction to the final index. Boundary lifting fills it, retaining all previously prescribed faces. This produces the composition, identity and higher compatibilities as transformations on $E_I$, rather than inferring them from pointwise uniqueness.

source.place: Opening compactification choice: the higher comparison coherence uses existing boundary lifting, Kerodon 00ZP.

proof.text: For a nonempty filtered category $J$, [lem-cbc-filtered-nerve-weak-contractibility] and [lem-cbc-simplicial-groupoid-localization] give $\Delta_J:\mathscr C\simeq E_J$. Choose a quasi-inverse $M_J$ and equivalence $\alpha:\Delta_JM_J\simeq\mathrm{id}_{E_J}$, and put $\beta=\alpha^{-1}$. For evaluation $e_j$, the equality $e_j\Delta_J=\mathrm{id}$ and the equivalence $e_j\alpha:M_J\simeq e_j$ yield $\Delta_Je_j\simeq\mathrm{id}$ by composing $\Delta_J(e_j\alpha)^{-1}$ with $\alpha$. Thus every evaluation is an inverse equivalence also in the filtered case.

source.place: Opening compactification choice: filtered nerve and the evaluation inverse equations.

proof.text:
For $F\in E_J$, the cocone $\beta_F:F\to\Delta_JM_JF$ has mapping-space map
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathscr C}(M_JF,x)\xrightarrow{\Delta_J}\operatorname{Map}_{E_J}(\Delta_JM_JF,\Delta_Jx)\xrightarrow{-\circ\beta_F}\operatorname{Map}_{E_J}(F,\Delta_Jx).$$
Full faithfulness gives the first equivalence, and precomposition with $\alpha_F$ is inverse to the second. Fullness of $E_J$ identifies the last space with the ambient functor mapping space. The cocone criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes this cocone colimiting. Its structure maps are equivalences by componentwise detection. The full subcategory of initial objects of its cocone category is nonempty and contractible by the same calculus. Every other colimiting cocone is equivalent to this one, so all its structure maps are equivalences too. For $t:F\to H$, the naturality equation is $\Delta_J(M_Jt)\beta_F\simeq\beta_Ht$, with the higher simplices of $\beta$.

source.place: Opening compactification choice: explicit filtered cocone universal property and naturality.

proof.text: For $u:H\to J$ between nonempty filtered categories, restrict $\beta_F$ to $u^*F\to\Delta_HM_JF$. Full faithfulness of $\Delta_H$ from step 10 and precomposition by this equivalence give the two equivalences in the factorization of step 11 with $H$ in place of $J$. Hence this restricted cocone is colimiting. Equivalent cocones remain equivalent after restriction, so every colimiting cocone on $F$ is preserved. Set $P=E_J$ in a containing universe. The restricted cocone with apex $M_J$ and the chosen cocone with apex $M_Hu^*$ are pointwise colimiting on the universal $H$-diagram. The pointwise colimit clause of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] makes them colimiting in $\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathscr C)$. Their full initial-object subcategory is contractible Kan by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Its mapping space gives the cone-compatible equivalence $M_Hu^*\to M_J$, natural on all of $P$.

source.place: Opening compactification choice: filtered restriction and parameterized cocone comparison, using the existing pointwise theorem.

proof.text: For a string of filtered index functors, restrict all the cocones and comparisons of step 12 to its last indexing category. They are objects and edges in the full initial-object subcategory on the resulting universal diagram in $\operatorname{Fun}(E_J,\mathscr C)$. Restriction composes degree by degree by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. That subcategory is a contractible Kan complex by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], so its map to $\Delta^0$ is a trivial Kan fibration by [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion]. As in step 9, boundary lifting supplies the composition triangle and then all higher simplices with previously fixed faces; identity edges are degenerate. These are coherent comparisons of natural transformations, with the colimit variance $M_Hu^*\to M_J$.

source.place: Opening compactification choice: filtered comparison coherence via the same boundary-filling theorem.

proof.text: For any enhanced parameter category $P$ small in the chosen sufficiently large universe, [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] permits $\mathscr C=\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathscr D)$. Every previous step applies to this category itself: $\alpha_F$ is then an equivalence of enhanced functors, so its cones and projections are coherent natural transformations in the parameter. Evaluation at a parameter sends this equivalence cone to an equivalence cone on an equivalence-arrow diagram, which is limiting by the calculation of step 4, and by step 11 in the filtered case. All constructions stay within the universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The nonempty hypothesis was used in step 1 and the equivalence-arrow hypothesis in step 2, so no empty-index or noninvertible-arrow assertion is obtained.
